title: Convert legacy admin runbooks into idempotent saga tasklets with safety rails
creator: Ava Nguyen
description: Migrate a selected set of high-frequency admin runbooks into a new runbook-as-task pipeline that treats each runbook as a finite-state saga composed of idempotent tasklets. The pipeline will provide: (1) automatic conversion shims for common admin scripts (bash/python) into typed tasklets with input validation and compensating actions, (2) in-situ dry-run simulation and canary execution modes, (3) built-in RBAC/audit hooks that emit structured events to the console and audit logs, and (4) runtime safety rails that can automatically pause or rollback on policy violations or abnormal telemetry. Goal is to reduce mean time to remediate (MTTR) for routine operator flows and make oncall execution reproducible and auditable.
acceptance_criteria: A conversion shim converts at least three canonical runbooks (db-rotate-keys, evacuate-node, clear-cache) into tasklet DAGs that are idempotent and have explicit compensating steps.
Dry-run mode simulates all external side effects and produces a deterministic execution plan used by review before run, with a link to the simulation trace in the console.
Task execution emits structured telemetry (trace id, step id, user, start/end, token consumption estimate) to the ops dashboard and audit log backend.
Auto-safety triggers (rate-limit exceeded, unexpected error spike, policy match) pause further progression and surface a suggested rollback action; documented in the runbook UI.
Security review signoff completed and RBAC integration tested with two enterprise tenants in a staging VPC.
Operator UX: oncall can run the converted runbook as a single-click action with optional interactive prompts; success/failure states mapped to SLOs in the dashboard.
Performance: typical converted runbook startup overhead < 150ms and step latency within existing SLO for same operator action.
Unit and integration tests covering happy path, compensating path, and simulated failure injection are present in the repo with CI passing.
Documentation and runbook pages published: conversion guide, developer API for tasklets, and ops-runbook migration checklist.
Rollback playbooks created for each migrated flow and validated via dry-run and staged execution in staging cluster.

implementation_notes: Design: Use Saga pattern where each step declares an optional compensating step and a side-effect descriptor (idempotency-key, target-resource, action-type).
Conversion shim: conservative approach—only convert idempotent-friendly commands automatically; others require an annotation and manual compensating step from the runbook author.
Telemetry: leverage existing ops-trace ingestion; emit a minimal structured event for each step to reduce cardinality. Include step-level token cost estimate for later cost attribution.
Safety rails: policy engine uses declarative rules in repo (yaml) evaluated pre-step; violations pause execution and notify via Slack and console modal.
RBAC: enforce both UI-level gating and server-side service token checks; admin passthrough disallowed except with explicit audit exemption that creates an auditable justification entry.

Tradeoffs: Full automatic conversion of arbitrary scripts is impossible; we prioritize a guided semi-automated flow to prevent unsafe transformations. This increases reviewer work but reduces incident risk.
Testing: add chaos tests that inject network/permission errors and verify compensating steps execute and system returns to safe state.
Performance: keep shim lightweight (single binary) and avoid loading heavy runtime libraries during task startup to meet 150ms target.
